transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Lincoln! I've been riding for a week handling depositions in Bloomington, trusting you to mind the office, and I come back to this! The Henderson deposition is gone — I cannot find it anywhere on your desk or mine. Judge Davis's letter has been sitting here unopened for five days! You told me you'd keep things in order while I was away!

*throws hat down on the desk*

What in blazes have you been doing all week? Do you have any idea how important that Henderson case is? We're due in court in three days, and without that deposition we'll look like fools before the judge!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Well, now, Mr. Herndon, I reckon I owe you an explanation for the state of affairs in the office. I must admit that I did not tend to matters as diligently as I ought to have whilst you were away. It appears that the Henderson deposition has gone astray, and Judge Davis's missive has lingered unanswered for a number of days. For this, I must apologize.

Please allow me a moment to gather my thoughts and consider how best to remedy the situation. Let us not be disheartened just yet, for there may yet be a solution to be found. Would you be so kind as to give me a brief moment to search for the missing deposition? Perhaps it has found its way into a different stack of papers or a drawer inadvertently.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*paces angrily across the office*

A brief moment? A BRIEF MOMENT? Lincoln, we don't have moments to spare! This isn't some minor contract dispute — the Hendersons stand to lose their entire property if we cannot produce that deposition proving the original deed was recorded in McLean County!

*gestures wildly at the cluttered desk*

And you sit there as calm as Sunday morning, talking about how it "may have found its way" somewhere! Papers don't just wander off on their own accord! You've been stuffing correspondence in your hat again, haven't you? Or using important documents as bookmarks in those infernal poetry volumes you keep around?

*picks up Judge Davis's unopened letter*

And this! Judge Davis doesn't write unless it's urgent. He's probably wondering why we haven't responded to whatever matter he's raised. Do you understand how this makes our firm look? How this makes ME look, when I've vouched for you keeping order?

Search if you must, but I want answers, Lincoln! What exactly WERE you doing all week if not minding the practice?

transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I understand the gravity of the situation and the importance of the Henderson case. I apologize for my lack of attention to detail and organization during your absence. It was not my intention to cause such distress or risk to our clients.

I must admit that I have not been as diligent in my duties as I should have been. I take full responsibility for the disarray in the office and the missing deposition. I assure you that I have not been using important documents as bookmarks or storing them in my hat. I have allowed the office to become disorganized, and for that, I am truly sorry.

As for how I spent my time while you were away, I must confess that I did not prioritize the tasks that needed to be done here in the office. I allowed distractions to pull me away from the important work that needed to be completed. It was a lapse in judgment on my part, and I deeply regret the consequences of my actions.

I am committed to making amends and ensuring that we address the issues at hand promptly. Let us work together to locate the missing deposition, respond to Judge Davis's letter, and prepare thoroughly for the upcoming court appearance. I value your trust and will do everything in my power to regain your confidence in my abilities.

transcript.text:
*stops pacing and stares at Lincoln incredulously*

"Distractions pulled you away"? What kind of answer is that? Lincoln, I need specifics! Were you off arguing politics at the statehouse again? Telling your endless stories down at the general store? What distractions could possibly be more important than our clients' livelihoods?

*slams hand on desk*

You speak of making amends and working together, but that doesn't tell me where the Henderson deposition IS! Mrs. Henderson came to this office in tears, trusting us to save her family's farm. Her husband's been dead two years, and that land is all she has to feed her children. And you let me ride off to Bloomington believing you'd protect her interests!

*voice rising*

I don't need your apologies right now, Lincoln — I need that deposition! Did you file it somewhere? Did you take it home? Did someone come by the office and collect it? Think, man! When was the last time you actually SAW it?

And these distractions you mention — if you're going to apologize, at least have the courtesy to tell me what was so all-fired important that you couldn't keep your mind on our practice! I deserve that much honesty, don't I?

*voice becoming slightly hoarse from shouting*

I need you to THINK, Lincoln! Close your eyes and picture this office last week. Picture yourself at your desk. What were you working on? What files were open? Where did you last SEE the Henderson deposition?

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln admits to engaging in 'political discussions or shared stories' and holding court at taverns, but also spent time alone with books and newspapers rather than seeking constant social interaction.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Throughout intense confrontation, Lincoln repeatedly apologizes, takes full responsibility, validates Herndon's anger ('I understand your frustration'), and never becomes defensive or argumentative despite harsh criticism.
